references.text: Moses took the wave offerings from their hands and burned them on the altar along with the burnt offering. This was the ordination offering, as described in the instructions for the consecration of priests.
The burnt offering is described as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, an offering made by fire—the same terminology used in Leviticus 8:28.
The burnt offering on the altar as a pleasing aroma (ריח ניחח) to the Lord is a recurring theme in the laws of sacrifice.
The priest burns the offering on the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The expression 'an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (אשה ריח ניחח ליהוה) is repeated here.
Aaron's sons burn the offering on the altar along with the burnt offering as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Summary of the laws of sacrifice including the ordination offering (מלואים), using the same words found in 8:28.
Moses burned the ram on the altar as a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire for the Lord—part of the same consecration ceremony.
Christ gave himself for us as a gift and a sacrifice to God, a pleasing aroma—a typological fulfillment of Old Testament sacrifices.
Paul describes the gift from the Philippians as a pleasing aroma, an offering that God receives with joy—language drawn from Old Testament sacrificial practices.
